## feature

## fix

### Adjacent insertion operations lost sequence

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: silent sequence loss in merged output. `build_read_structure` walked
the raw record CIGAR and keyed insertions by reference boundary, so
adjacent `I` ops overwrote each other.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`build_read_structure` normalizes the record CIGAR (`normalize_cigar`)
before the walk, matching what discovery already does — adjacent identical
ops merge into one event carrying all bases.

#### before

```text
merged cigar=10M3I10M   (2 of 5 inserted bases lost)
```

#### after

```text
merged cigar=10M5I10M   seq carries all 5 inserted bases, NM:i:5, MD:Z:20
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_merge.py::TestIndels::test_adjacent_insertion_ops_merge_all_bases`.
:::

### SAM '=' SEQ shorthand corrupted statistics and NM/MD

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: silent statistics loss (masked observations dropped as ineligible)
and consensus corruption (every masked base degraded to N@Q2, NM inflated
to the read length).

#### description

```
type: text
```

New `expand_reference_matches` resolves aligned `=` characters against the
reference before discovery and structure building (no-op when the sequence
has no `=`; clipped/inserted `=` stays literal — no reference counterpart).
Called in `_both_mapped` and `_adjust_single`. One implementation subtlety:
pysam's `query_sequence` setter drops `query_qualities`; they are captured
and restored explicitly.

#### before

```text
merged NM=20 (correct: 1)   MD=0C0C0C0T0A0C0T0A0T0C0G0A0T0T0T0A0A0C0G0C5
```

#### after

```text
disagreement rows: 1 (pos 516, alt C, dp 2)   merged NM=1  MD=15A9
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_merge.py::TestEqualsShorthand::test_equals_seq_shorthand_resolved`.
The intermediate `qualities_missing` failure during development is itself
evidence the qualities-restore is required.
:::

### Symlinked output directories bypassed collision checks

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: two outputs could share one physical file through an aliased
directory — publication failed and left Parquet content at the BAM
destination.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`_check_distinct_outputs` compares `os.path.realpath` for duplicates and
input collisions (resolves parent-directory symlinks even for files that
do not exist yet); `samefile` remains for existing paths.

#### before

```text
exit=1; content at the BAM destination starts with b'PAR1'
```

#### after

```text
exit=2; adjusted_bam and disagreement_parquet resolve to the same file: …/real/same
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_cli.py::TestPathValidation::test_symlinked_output_dirs_collide_rejected`.
:::

### Colocated mates were judged by read number

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: identical physical alignments merged or failed purely on which
mate was read1 — an orientation-validity decision read numbering cannot
support.

#### description

```
type: text
```

New shared `leftmost_is_read1` helper: distinct starts by coordinate;
equal starts by orientation model (`fr`: forward mate leftmost, `rf`:
reverse mate, otherwise read1). Used by both `select_pair` and
`try_merge`; TLEN and clip-owner tie rules are unaffected.

#### before

```text
r1_fwd=True:  merged=1
r1_fwd=False: merged=0   (orientation_incompatible)
```

#### after

```text
r1_fwd=True:  merged=1
r1_fwd=False: merged=1
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_merge.py::TestColocatedOrientationTie::test_orientation_tie_independent_of_read_number`
(both strand variants merge; existing colocated FR tests unchanged).
:::

## limitation

### '=' without a reference counterpart stays literal

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: documented edge; clips and insertions have no reference position to
resolve against.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`=` characters inside soft clips or insertions remain literal in the
record; consensus eligibility treats them like any non-ACGT character.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
None
:::

## caveat

### '=' expansion mutates the in-flight record sequence

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: intended and documented; noted so record-mutation auditing is not
surprised.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Records whose primaries are processed carry the expanded sequence in the
outputs (unmapped and non-primary records pass through untouched, literal
`=` included).

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Pinned by the shorthand regression test; README states the rule.
:::

## observation

### Benchmark measured on a loaded machine; A/B shows no code regression

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the committed absolute numbers are slower than history; the
context prevents a wrong conclusion later.

#### description

```
type: table
```

| Measurement | Time | Throughput |
| ----------- | ---- | ---------- |
| Historical (idle machine) | 7.6–7.8 s | 2,562–2,643 pairs/s |
| Pre-batch, this session (load avg ~10) | 9.0 s | 2,227 pairs/s |
| Post-batch, this session (load avg ~10) | 8.7–11.1 s | 1,801–2,300 pairs/s |

The pre/post A/B ran under the same load within minutes of each other
(pre-batch via `git stash`); the batch is not the cause of the slowdown.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: table
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
`uptime` showed load average 10.43/10.03/9.08 during the runs; the A/B
pair (9.0 s pre vs 8.7 s post) is the comparable measurement.
:::
